subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make global policy the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent security policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistent session overrides
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or patch session fields to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset or doctor repair first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing reset or doctor repair path before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make global policy the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent security policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override feature, resolver tests, and exec-default layering points to this account.
